exclude: Source pages copied byte for byte into the scorecard printer part
Source pages copied byte for byte into the scorecard printer part
Unchanged staging twin of $D000–$D553 at the tee, copied by $BF50 before the hole load
Byte-for-byte copy of the KERNAL vector table at the same addresses

comments.text: Fractional byte of the lateral aim coordinate, updated with carries into $0D64.
The stick poll combines active directions and fire with the caller's pending value.
Synthetic control bits selected by the demo stage machine. The gameplay controller uses them when the demo stage is active and there is no live input.
Current animation frame index used by the raster pose update.
Incremented from the CIA swing timer while a swing timing phase is active.
Phase selector for the power and snap timer paths. Zero leaves the swing updates idle.
Zero-based player index chosen by the turn-order routine.
Selects the bitmap font base through the tables at $5FD5 and $5FD9.
Set by fire at $15C1 and cleared after pose $1F by the animation routine.
Set by $160F on the first snap fire press.
Set when the fire release is captured for this stroke.
Stores the timing-derived snap index used by the launch and in-flight calculations.
Current club selection. The full shot path cycles across thirteen indices with the stick.
Timing-derived power value latched by the release handler and used by the launch calculation.
High byte of the lateral aim coordinate, paired with zero-page $3F.
Jumps into the resident engine initializer at $14BA.
Stops CIA1 timer A, clears pending CIA interrupts and installs the handler at $0E39 through $0314. Enables the VIC raster source at line $FB and enables CPU interrupts.

Acknowledges the VIC and tests its raster flag. On raster interrupts it advances the software timers, updates the golfer's sprite pose and calls the ball coordinate integrator. Other interrupts go through $101D. Restores Y, X and A before RTI.

Walks the 16 active flags at $0DA9 backwards. Active slots decrement their countdowns at $0DB9 and reload from $0D98 on expiry. Slot 15 also updates the frame counters and conditionally toggles the low bit of sprite 0 colour.
Ignores disabled animation and unchanged pose indices. Saves a new index from $82, selects sprite blocks and positions for that pose, then uses its low two bits to select the final update path.
Chooses six sprite pointers from one of two groups according to bit 1 of $82, adds bit 0 to each and writes them at $63F8–$63FD.
Two groups of six VIC sprite indices. The pose updater adds the low bit of the current pose to each index.
Uses the pose index in $82 to look up VIC sprite coordinates. The first X and Y stores are $0F1E and $0F24.
32 X coordinates for sprite 0 indexed by pose.
32 Y coordinates for sprite 0 indexed by pose.

Looks up the frame stream by X and the destination half by Y. Clears one 256-byte page per section, then reads pairs of pixel byte and destination offset. A zero ends the section and a second zero ends the frame packet.
Low destination bytes for the sprite expander, indexed by Y.
High destination bytes select $6B00 or $6800 for swing frames.
Low bytes of the frame stream pointers used by the sprite expander.
High bytes of the frame stream pointers used by the sprite expander.
Tests for a CIA1 timer A interrupt. During a swing, polls the timing stages, increments $85 and updates the indicator before rearming the timer.
During swing timing phase 1 with the power-release latch clear, polls for release. Advances the highlighted nibble through two meter tiles when the timing value is below 16.
In phase 2 while fire remains held, restores part of the two power meter tiles as the timing value advances from 16 through 31.
In phase 2, writes the marker nibble to the appropriate meter tile from timing 16 onward.
In the third swing timing phase, polls for snap and writes the snap bitmap marker until the input is latched or the timing window ends.
Selects escape byte $FF and the glyph buffer as destination, then joins the common row runs decoder.
Gets the row address in screen RAM from the row pointer tables and uses the common run-length row decoder.
Gets the colour RAM destination for the current row and enters the $44-escape decode path.
Decodes single values or escape, repeat count, value triples. Writes up to forty cells and advances the compressed source pointer for the next row.
Multiplies the glyph index in A by eight and adds the table base selected by $8E. Patches its own immediate operands from the low and high base arrays and returns the glyph address in $FB–$FC.
Banks in the KERNAL, enables keyboard row outputs, then calls SCNKEY and GETIN. Returns the resulting PETSCII byte in A after restoring port $35. A nonzero byte also goes to $AD32.

Saves both CIA1 data directions and makes both ports inputs. Reads port 2 through $DC00, inverts the active-low signals and ORs the five control bits into $80 when there is input. Restores both direction registers before returning.
Copies CIA1 data direction registers to $FB and $FC for the stick poll.
Writes $FC and $FB back to CIA1 port B and A directions and reads back both ports.
Clears bit 0 of CIA1 control register A, preserving the other bits.
Sets bits 0 and 3 of CIA1 control register A to start timer A in one-shot mode.
Copies eight bytes from the source at ($FB) to the bitmap destination at ($FD). The usual entry sets Y to 7.
Uses A as a mask of sprite positions whose X high bits should be cleared in $D010. Restores A.
ORs A into the VIC sprite enable register and restores A.
Reads every address in the $FE and $FF pages with the KERNAL visible and writes the bytes back into underlying RAM.
Sets the NMI vector and CIA directions, copies the interrupt pages, selects VIC bank $4000 and multicolour bitmap mode, clears audio and initializes the default names and skills.
Clears per-round working state, configures the timer and resets the current player and hole indices before jumping to the load sequence at $1946.
Saves $39 and $0D0B across clearance of the game RAM and zero-page work areas.
Zeros $39–$70, $D1–$F2 and $73–$8F, including shot and temporary coordinates.
Clears the pending stick bits and polls port 2. If fire is held, sets the swing animation flag at $0D00.
Changes the club index on up or down and wraps it through 0–12. Redraws the club indication, arms a repeat delay and stores the club for the active player.
If the snap flag is clear, samples the stick and latches the first fire press. Stores the low nibble of timing byte $85 at $0D05 below $2F, or $0E from $2F onward.
While the release flag is clear, waits for the fire bit to clear. Latches the release and converts timing byte $85 to the power value at $0D07, with different rules before and after $10.
Refills four eight-byte meter positions with $AA, restores the marker bytes and clears the ball-in-motion and swing input flags.
Steps the pose index when the animation timer expires. Uses a per-pose delay table, calls phase handlers at selected indices and clears the swing flag at index $20.
Thirty-two render tick durations, indexed by pose and passed to the animation timer.
Disables sprites 0–5, loads their starting coordinate pairs and pointers, sets their colours, and resets the pose and previously drawn pose to zero.
Converts the low yardage byte at $937F to decimal, then adds the digit corrections indexed by $9380. Replaces leading zeroes with the blank glyph and draws in the status panel.

Loads the TF file selected for the course, copies its staged data into RAM beneath I/O and loads the hole file. Offers retry on disk errors. After a successful load it reads par at $C557 and transfers control to the hole loop.
Increments the zero-based hole index and reloads while the result is below 18. At 18 it offers the print path, checks the round limit and either resets the hole index for the next round or restarts.
XORs each of ten bytes from $1A05 with $FF and writes the result at $FF58–$FF61. This supplies the RAM interrupt dispatch while the KERNAL is hidden.
Bytewise complements of the ten-byte interrupt stub installed at $FF58.
Selects the active player's club from $0D1F, initialises shot and golfer display state, then polls aim and shot input while awaiting a stroke.
Advances the putting pose when the raster timer expires, sets the four changing sprite pointers, and calls the launch routine at pose 6. Clears the active flag at pose 10.
Loads five pages of the putting animation from frame packet 16. Sets the sprite pointers, positions, colours and initial putting state.
Sets the play text bank and draws 25 rows of the bitmap layout, colour layer and third template layer in separate passes.
Draws the putting controls and golfer, polls aim and fire until the stroke starts, then updates ball projection, ground drag and sound until the putt and its animation finish.
Checks ball height, distance from the reference point and bitmap pixels below the ball. Decrements the ground movement multiplier up to four times when the ball requires the drag adjustment.
Restores the eight-by-eight meter glyph bytes and the eight initial timing marker bytes in the bitmap.
Enters only while fire is pressed. Draws the initial eight putt meter positions, then times the remaining fire hold in two-tick intervals and remembers the level when fire is released.
Builds the right-side bitmap panel, sets up its colours and writes successive strips of glyphs from the panel table.
Two 48-byte groups of source pixel pairs used by the green marker overlay.
Reads a per-group count and paired start coordinates from the hole data. Expands signed X and Y deltas into split low and high coordinate lists with a separate destination for each shape group.
Puts the decoded hole record address $C554 in $FB–$FC.
Returns the pair X:Y pointing to $C558 in the decoded hole header.
Returns the pair X:Y pointing to $C559 in the decoded hole header.
Returns the hole header pointer $C557 in X and Y.
Computes a byte offset of sixteen times $0D7B plus twice $45 and returns it in $FB–$FC.
Loads the record count from $C55C, hides I/O to access RAM, and scatters successive four-byte records into the indexed columns at $BB92, $BC52, $BD12 and $BDD2.

Walks each decoded boundary group, shifts coordinates relative to the player and applies the current golf projection unless overhead mode is selected. Writes transformed vertices back to the working column arrays.
Walks the terrain record columns backwards, rotates their points into the player view unless overhead mode is set and applies the lower depth bound before storing them.
Forms the two components of a coordinate transform from inputs at $D1–$D4 and coefficients at $75–$78. Multiplies and rescales each term before subtracting into $D5–$D6 and adding into $D7–$D8.
Reflects the phase in A:Y into the first quadrant, fetches neighbouring 16-bit table entries and interpolates using the low phase byte. Negates the result for the negative half-cycle.
Sixty-four little-endian values approaching zero from $7FFF. The quarter-wave routine and its inverse angle search use adjacent entries for interpolation.
Computes squared distance between two course points, adding the squares of the signed X and Z separations into $28F4–$28F7.

Uses successive averages of a trial value and squared distance divided by that value. When the trial stops decreasing, adds the discarded half bit and returns that estimate in X and Y. Inputs zero and one take the A-return path.
Uses the coordinate delta and distance to form a scaled ratio, searches the quarter-wave table and interpolates the angle between adjacent entries.

Clears putting state and VIC sprite enables, sets default coordinates and builds the opening view for a golfer who has yet to play. Takes the saved-state path at $293B when that player's flag in $2A1D is set.
Resolves the word in X:Y into two scaled components using the coefficients generated from angle $42:$43. Writes one result at $46–$47 and one at $28F2–$28F3.
Sets launch velocity through the short shot path selected by $3BE6. This path is used when both the skill threshold and terrain check allow it.

Converts the selected polygon group into projected edges at successively higher trial heights. When a clipped case is flagged, reruns the edge builder at reference height and fills the resulting visible span.
Draws the selected polygon in descending height slices from $18 toward $10, then handles the clipped fill path at height $10.
Projects pairs of vertices at the current height, saves each point's outcode and full coordinates, then calls the clipped line path and advances around the polygon.

Steps from the two endpoint coordinates along the dominant axis, using the distance accumulator to step the other axis. Hands each pixel inside the 120-by-200 course area to the selected segment painter.
Given bitmap pixel coordinates in X and Y, selects its row base, cell and scanline. Patches both operands used by the pixel plotting routine and saves the two-bit pixel index.
Exchanges the endpoints, high coordinates, outcodes and clipping work fields. Records the swap at $0D88.
Projects successive polygon vertices, wraps the endpoint index to zero, clips the edge and dispatches visible segments.
Calls the edge-record insertion routine, advances the record count and returns to the edge loop.

Rejects segments by their group flags and current pass, then paints along a projected bitmap row. The paths for type 2, type 3 and other types use different fill masks and tests against the existing pixels.
Selects bitmap pixel masks and fills along the span for the type-2 path, using $AA for eligible whole bytes.
Selects the current bitmap masks and writes eligible pixels for the general span path, using $55 for eligible whole bytes.
Compares the current, previous and next vertex rows. Uses the relative X direction and neighbouring row signs to choose edge treatment flags at $0C80.
Checks the left and right screen limits for an odd count of selected edge flags. Inserts a bottom edge marker when needed so the later fill has a paired boundary.

Clears the three sprite pages at $6400–$66FF and draws the small marker shapes. Sets sprite 6 coordinates and the initial aim coordinate to $1800, then calls the aim updater, which can leave sprite 7 coordinates unchanged when its latch is set.
Immediate operand of the sprite mask load at $3638. The conditional patch near $98F4 can write this byte.

Checks shot state and the update latch, then reads the stick. Left and right subtract or add one to the 16-bit aim coordinate at $0D64:$3F, with bounds depending on skill and play state. Projects the aim and updates sprite 7 coordinates.
Sets up putt parameters, collects the starting screen position, then sets $0D3C and $7D to enable coordinate integration and shot processing.
Uses the shot meter index in X to select a repeat count and adds the club-indexed value at $3844 that many times. Index 7 or a zero player flag selects zero. Stores the result at $0D3D.
Fifteen repeat counts indexed by the snap position. Count zero is the neutral entry at index 7.
Club-indexed increments used when turning the snap index into a movement component.
Stores 8 in the two meter fields at $0D9E and $0DBF and enables their update flag at $0DAF.
Combines club-indexed values with the shot parameters, calls the multiplication routine, then saves the products in the split velocity fields $3E:$E7 and $3D:$E6.
Handles vertical contact with the reference height, scales velocities at impact and updates ground movement while the relevant timer is idle.
Copies ball sprite Y to shadow sprite Y and clears the shot-in-progress flag when all three velocities are zero.
Copies the two horizontal velocity words to their landing work fields before clearing the vertical velocity.
Advances lateral velocity according to snap index when vertical velocity is nonzero, applies the stored wind components off the reference height, and decreases vertical velocity by $26 on its timer.
Projects the ball and its reference-height position. Updates sprite 6 and 7 X, sets their high X bits from the screen offset carry and writes separate Y coordinates when the ball is off the tee.

When $0D3C is set, divides each signed velocity by the update divisor at $0D50. Carries the leftover fraction forward in $0D46,X and adds or subtracts the whole increment from the corresponding ball coordinate. Preserves the interrupted routine's arithmetic workspace.
Derives distance and projected offsets from aim and reference coordinates, then scales the shot velocity into two horizontal components saved for the landing update.
Checks motion and the height bound, then compares depth and lateral offsets with the cup location. Selects a capture threshold from the lateral difference.

Checks the putt speed, reference height and position fraction. If within the capture thresholds it hides the ball sprites and stops integration. Otherwise the response depends on the terrain and player skill fields.
Negates the two-byte lateral deflection when the saved cup-side flag is negative.
Converts course coordinates to the overhead screen position with divisors $30 and $80. Returns the result around the horizontal and vertical reference points in X and Y.
On T, if its state check allows, disables sprites and switches projection, redraws hole geometry and terrain, and waits for another T. Re-enters the normal hole setup on return.
Fills the 30-cell-wide course area over 25 rows with alternating $CC and $33 bitmap bytes.
Clears the marker sprite page, builds the shapes and configures the sprites. Sprite 0 uses the active golfer's saved coordinates. Sprites 1 and 2 share the position projected from $2A21–$2A24.
Sets the panel font, draws the 36-glyph row from $BE92 and clears input while switching the display into setup.
High bytes of glyph table bases indexed by $8E and copied into the operand at $1248.
Low bytes of glyph table bases indexed by $8E and copied into the operand at $1242.
High bytes of the five layout addresses read by $B821.
Low bytes of the five 90-byte panel layouts.
Aiming and ball marker sprite pages cleared and populated by $3638.
VIC sprite bitmap frames at indices $A0–$B7 in bank $4000. Sprites 0–5 use this area while golfing. The PRNT load replaces these same addresses with the scorecard printer.
Second 256-byte sprite work page at $6900. The frame decoder clears it and fills selected byte offsets.
Remaining bytes of the second 256-byte sprite buffer used by the sparse frame decoder.
Third 256-byte sprite work page at $6A00. The frame decoder populates it from the tail of a swing frame packet.
First page of the upper sprite work half. The expander selects this half with Y = 0.
Second page of the upper sprite work half at $6C00.
Third page of the upper sprite work half at $6D00.
Golfer frame packet 0, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 86, 84, 71 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 1, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 102, 90, 58 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 2, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 120, 95, 68 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 3, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 120, 95, 64 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 4, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 122, 91, 47 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 5, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 131, 93, 37 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 6, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 134, 91, 57 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 7, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 125, 81, 74 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 8, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 93, 85, 66 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Continuation of frame packet 8 from $7ED0 across the ledger boundary at $8000.
Golfer frame packet 9, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 88, 84, 71 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 10, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 107, 92, 50 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 11, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 117, 95, 37 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 12, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 134, 96, 40 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 13, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 138, 96, 52 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 14, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 138, 90, 68 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Golfer frame packet 15, decoded by $0F83. Writes 3 sprite pages with 138, 92, 70 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Putting golfer packet 16, decoded by $0F83. Writes 5 sprite pages with 111, 65, 53, 46, 73 byte-offset pairs, respectively.
Reads the requested sprite's X and Y registers including the high X bit and applies the viewport offset. Returns the bitmap X and Y coordinates.
Uses Y for bitmap row and scanline and X for four-pixel cell and pixel position. Writes the destination pointer and masks and returns the scanline offset in Y.
Uses the high and low distance bytes to select a display scale and divisor of 1, 12 or 36. Saves the scaled value and scale index.
Computes and projects marker endpoints around the ball. Uses a short path for lower skill levels in the default terrain state and draws a series of slope segments on the alternate path.
Projects a pair of height endpoints and draws their screen segment. Saves screen coordinates for the selected indicator row.
Stores A in $AE. If A is nonzero and putting flag $8F is clear, adds the low bit of $0DC8.
Fills eleven 240-byte bitmap strips, installs five object coordinates and draws the fixed set of terrain objects for the range view.
Uses the demo stage at $3A and shot index at $F1 to choose virtual stick commands. Advances through club selection, aim, fire and timing checks and writes the synthetic stick value at $81.
Multiplies X and Y using the shared multiply workspace at $5B–$60, returning the product low byte in A and high byte in X.
Selects current ball, reference height or aim coordinates with X, or uses the overhead projection when $0D97 is set. Returns screen X in X, screen Y in Y and off-screen flags in A.
Shift-and-add multiplies the two words at $5B–$5C and $5F–$60 over 16 steps, leaving the 32-bit product in $5B–$5E.
Converts both 16-bit operands to magnitudes, multiplies them and negates the four-byte product when their original signs differ.
Divides the word at $63–$64 by the word at $61–$62 using sixteen shift-and-subtract iterations. Returns quotient at $63–$64, remainder at $65–$66 and carry set for zero divisor.

Records operand signs, divides their magnitudes, and gives the quotient the sign of the operand XOR and the remainder the sign of the dividend. On zero divisor it clears quotient and remainder and returns carry set.
Prepares a signed 32-bit dividend at $63–$66 and a signed 16-bit divisor at $61–$62 for the shared division loop. Returns via the common sign restoration path.
Sets the panel font and builds all 25 rows of the setup bitmap and colour layout using the three template passes.
Records the hole strokes and accumulates par. Sums score bytes separately for the front and back nine for each configured player, keeping the carry in a separate high byte.
Compares the player's 16-bit score with accumulated par. Displays the magnitude with the over or under sign glyph, or an even-par glyph on equality.
Draws front-nine strokes for the selected golfer from the card table, stopping at the current hole or at the nine-hole subtotal.
Draws back-nine strokes and totals for the selected golfer once the hole index is at least nine.
Walks the recorded strokes through the current hole, compares each to its par byte and writes colour pairs for under-par or over-par scores.
Selects the player name base at $A11E, sets the stride to eight and shares the indexed pointer arithmetic at $9EF4.
Repeatedly divides by 1000, 100 and 10 to split the 16-bit value at $63–$64 into the four digit bytes at $A13F–$A142.
Calls the name display helper, which returns early on the driving range. Sets the active golfer's panel marker and renders the configured players' stroke counts.
Looks up the glyph, flips every bit in its eight bitmap bytes and writes them to the chosen destination. Advances the text cursor after the copy.
Converts the zero-based hole index to display digits and renders them with par read through the hole header pointer at $C557.
Draws the player setup screen, invokes the prompt and normal name and round entry, then initializes player records.
Uses successive rows 6–19 to draw the three parts of the setup panel with three pairs of values from the $5FE5–$5FFE parameter area.
Zeros the CIA time-of-day counters before polling keys at the player count prompt.
Enters the demo on D or when the time-of-day minute reaches one. Shift+Return invokes course selection, R enters the range and G the practice green. Digits 1–4 save a zero-based player count.
Disables VIC interrupts and sprites, banks in the KERNAL, masks CIA1 interrupts and stops its timers before calling SETLFS for device 8, secondary address $FF.
Calls SETNAM with the supplied length and filename pointer, then LOAD. Stores the carry-set result in $A2A4, reinstalls the game IRQ and leaves RAM visible under the KERNAL.
Writes zero to CIA1 hours, minutes, seconds and tenths in that order.
Writes zeros to $0D00–$0DC8.
Compares players' hole stroke counts to make ranks, breaks ties with their previous order and clears the hole counters once the order has been saved.

Looks for a golfer who has yet to take the first shot and matches the current honours rank. Then compares distance fields among golfers who are still in play. Advances the hole if the completion flags are all set.
Uses A times 64 to select the prompt and draws four 16-glyph rows.
Four-by-sixteen layout for the player number and name prompt in the setup glyph encoding. Blank cells use $94.
Four-by-sixteen layout for Professional, Amateur and Kids.
Four-by-sixteen layout for F1, F3, F5 and F7 and their corresponding hole counts.

Reads names for the configured player slots, allows up to eight letters or spaces and handles Delete and Return. Commits the eight encoded values to the current player's record and calls the skill prompt before moving on.
Eight values for the name being entered. Letters A–Z are stored as 30–55 and a space as 10.
Polls for P, A or K, translates to 2, 1 or 0 and saves the result in the current player skill table. Slash returns to setup.
Draws the round-length choices and waits for F1, F3, F5 or F7. Saves the chosen zero-based round count at $0D0B.
Renders the prompt player digit from the work byte at $3B plus glyph offset $97.
Projects the wind reference vector and draws the indicator. Uses the selected wind magnitude and direction to compute the two horizontal components kept at $A877–$A87A.
Writable immediate operand for the first line drawing mode. The wind panel caller temporarily writes 1 here before restoring zero.
Computes offsets from the active player's saved position, enables the wind value only for skill 2 and updates the status panel geometry.
Clears the coordinate integration flag, repositions sprite 6 and switches it to pointer $99. Uses the terrain and state flags to choose whether to display the sprite and clears the shot flag.
Walks through SID offsets 24 down to 0 and zeros every write register.
Clears SID, sets the volume and filter defaults, and applies the initial cutoff.
Sets both frequency registers to zero for all three SID voices.
Selects filter-route bit 1 before joining the common filter register write.
Selects filter-route bit 2 before joining the common filter register write.
Clears filter-route bit 0 before joining the filter register write.
Adds the signed adjustment at $AB70 to A with saturation at 0 or 255, writes the result to the SID cutoff high byte and copies the low byte from $AB6B.
Selects the SID voice with register offset seven times X. Loads frequency, pulse width, ADSR and control from per-voice tables before setting the waveform's gate bit.
Computes the SID voice register offset, clears the gate bit from its stored control value and writes the control register.
Sets up and gates on voice 2, starts timer slot ten, waits for the countdown and releases the gate.
Clears the sort and clipping work arrays, then repeatedly finds the deepest unprocessed point. Saves the ordered indices at $0AC0 and projects each object.
Skips points at insufficient depth or off screen. Projects the terrain object, selects the width tier and composites its canopy and companion masks at the resulting position.
Temporarily exposes RAM under I/O, scans one terrain shape mask, and combines selected source bits into the destination bitmap with the masks at $52 and $53.
Converts projected depth to a tier index with descending thresholds. For nearer tiers it uses the low bit of $ED to choose one of two neighbouring masks.
Reads the mask base from the low and high pointer tables, advances by strip index times strip width and returns the source bit mask for the remaining column offset.
Loads $C900 into the pointer at $FB–$FC.
Records projected shape bounds in one of two groups of screen-coordinate arrays, using the shape's type index and current render coordinates.

Checks clipping and state flags before walking the sorted course records. Compares ball depth and height with candidate objects, calls the overlap tests and updates $0D54 and the current collision state.
Reads the bitmap colour pair under the ball, then checks its four neighbours for the uniform-colour case and records a separate result code for it.
Samples the pixel under sprite 7 and checks neighbouring colours to distinguish the uniformly coloured case.
Updates launch velocity on the first object-contact path selected in $B03D. Uses the current input and collision record to set the post-contact velocity fields.
Clamps the forward velocity used for the rebound, converts a quarter of it to signed lateral velocity according to which side of the object the ball reached, and clears snap and wind adjustments.
Tests display bounds, swing phase and ground height before dispatching the terrain response. The stop path clears velocity integration and hides sprite 7.
Samples several positions near the recorded ball pixel to choose the ground transition result returned in carry.
Compares depth against the pin position and checks position and terrain around it. Updates the two high collision-state bits at $0D26.
Iterates over two 48-byte bitmap areas. Uses the source strip at $204A for position-specific substitutions where the old pixel matches the tested colour pair.

During timing phase 3 after tick $2A, checks whether the snap landed in the allowed interval for the current skill and terrain. On the exceptional branch, restores reference coordinates and sets the one-shot flag.
Copies the first thirty bytes of the current glyph row to the supplied indirect destination.
Selects a 90-byte glyph stream, copies it to the working table, shifts its display window and refreshes the panel.
Displays the course prompt, accepts A–Z and stores the selected letter at $A2A1 for the CT filename.
Uses X to select a sixteen-glyph string at $B8A9 and writes it into the play bitmap using the text bank selected by $8E = 3.
Sixteen-glyph prompt rows. The first four read NEW COURSE Y/N, INPUT COURSE, TURN DISK and ERROR RETRY Y/N.
Sixteen blank glyphs to clear the disk prompt after a successful selection.
Sixteen-glyph PRINT SCORES Y/N prompt used by the round-end branch.
Accepts Y or N after a round. Y opens the filename-letter prompt and loads the chosen course table. Slash transfers directly to round reset.
Polls the keyboard for a PETSCII letter A through Z and saves it as the first byte of the course table filename at $A2A1.
Selects DMO, RNG or a three-byte disk name from the course filename table according to the demo, practice and hole flags. Calls the shared named load routine.
Two adjacent three-byte filenames. DMO is selected for the demo and RNG for the driving range.
Chooses the leading letter from the demo, practice or per-hole course state. Writes the letter to $B9C9 and passes the three-byte buffer with its existing TF suffix to the shared loader.
Clears and recolours the first 30 cells of the course header. Translates PETSCII letters, digits and spaces from $BEE0 to the bitmap font and draws each glyph inverted.
Polls Y or N before requesting PRNT. Retries a failed load on Y, and jumps to $6800 after success.
Branches to the printer retry prompt on carry set. Falls through to RTS on success.
Calls the named disk loader with a four-byte filename, PRNT, pointed to by $BA92.
PETSCII filename requested by the scorecard print branch.
The 36-glyph caption laid out by $3FB3.
Thirty-character course title shown at the top of the hole view. The captured Cypress Creek title is padded with spaces.

Banks out I/O with $01 = $24 and copies twelve pages from $C000–$CBFF to $D000–$DBFF. Re-enables I/O with $01 = $25 before enabling interrupts.

Little-endian pointers to the delta-encoded boundary records. The reader at $21FB indexes these by group and boundary number.
Four-byte absolute starting coordinates for boundaries, addressed through the index at $21E6 before the signed deltas are accumulated.
Packed columns in row order before transposition by $2233. Each object occupies four bytes and the count comes from $C55C.
Jump entry for the game's resident KERNAL LOAD replacement.

Saves the high zero-page workspace, copies the SETNAM filename, and dispatches the resident printer or course request. Numbered holes normally rewrite to the course's 00 file and select a stream number before the drive transfer.
Hides ROM and I/O, copies four pages from $DC00–$DFFF and two from $FB00–$FCFF into $6800–$6DFF, then joins loader cleanup.
Prepares the rewritten filename and raster-sensitive transfer parameters, then sends the name to the drive via CIA2.
Reads the stream header and expands successive packed streams until the requested stream count is exhausted, then drains the transfer.
Restores the saved stack position and port, waits for the drive signal, then updates the course title for CT requests and joins loader cleanup.
Restores the sixteen saved zero-page bytes at $F0–$FF and returns through the status instruction at $CD54.
Mutable, zero-terminated filename used by the resident loader. Numbered hole requests generally replace the last two characters with 00.
Sends a byte MSB first as eight data bits on CIA2's serial port and preserves the calling X and Y values.
Reads the next byte from the serial buffer at $0500, refilling the buffer at its boundary. Wraps the read with flags saved on the stack.
Waits for the drive and uses raster timing to avoid a bad-line transfer. Collects the serial bits through CIA2 port A and stores successive reconstructed bytes in the page $0500.
Builds the variable-width length and offset tables and decodes literal bytes and prior-output back-references into the destination encoded in the stream.
Accumulates the requested number of bits, refilling the bit reservoir through the packed byte reader.
Clears the course caption strip, measures trailing spaces to centre the name, and copies eight bitmap rows per letter from the heading font.
Sixteen saved bytes for the resident loader to restore before returning to play.
